title: Exact Q-space free form for arbitrary finite-cutoff Gaussian wavefunctions

general_gaussian_formula.trial_class: In the real standard-Gaussian Q-space coordinates, let the modulus-squared density of a normalized Gaussian wavefunction be N(m,S), where m is arbitrary and S is any real symmetric positive-definite covariance; an arbitrary real linear-quadratic phase is allowed
general_gaussian_formula.density: rho_(m,S)(xi)=det(S)^(-1/2) exp[-(1/2)((xi-m)^T S^(-1)(xi-m)-xi^T xi)] relative to the standard Gaussian measure, and the positive amplitude is psi=rho^(1/2)
general_gaussian_formula.exact_amplitude_cost: For diagonal frequency matrix Omega, q0[psi]=(1/4){m^T Omega m+Tr[Omega(S+S^(-1)-2I)]}
general_gaussian_formula.matrix_positivity: S+S^(-1)-2I=(I-S)S^(-1)(I-S) is positive semidefinite, so the covariance and mean terms are nonnegative without requiring [S,Omega]=0
general_gaussian_formula.phase_guard: Multiplication by exp(i theta(xi)) adds int |grad theta|_Omega^2 rho with no cross term, so a real linear-quadratic Gaussian phase cannot lower the amplitude cost
general_gaussian_formula.diagonal_recovery: When S=diag(s_j), the trace term is sum_j omega_j(s_j-1)^2/s_j and exactly recovers K1524
general_gaussian_formula.scope_guard: This classifies finite-cutoff Gaussian Q-space wavefunctions with arbitrary mean, covariance and quadratic phase; it does not classify genuinely non-Gaussian vectors or construct a continuum Gaussian representation
